evidence: Candidate descends from frozen Xplorer source 78632b12eeb4e4123b1a767c8b815fe6617681f9 and protected backend, permission, audience, routing, map-state and creation surfaces were excluded from the redesign diff.
The tested candidate passed 926/926 Jest tests, every deterministic Xplorer verifier, and the production browser sweep across all 76 declared routes.
Map controls were reframed from internal filter mechanics into the human questions what are you looking for, when does it matter, and what should the map show.
Discover elevates the existing recommendation reason under an explicit Why it is here hierarchy before the next action.
The Experience Model connects before, discover, consider, trust, commit, prepare, participate, complete and remember/follow-up rather than treating 76 screens independently.
Shared navigation, map, Discover, Quick Access, startup framing and global theme consumers use one coherent service hierarchy, while the required whole-app prototype represents all 76 real routes.
The proven five persistent destinations remain News Feed, Messages, Map/Camera, Leaderboard and Profile; no capability was hidden behind a new unsupported IA.
Quick Access retains its permission-correct route filtering while grouping access as service areas and preserving orientation back to the current plan.
The first footer styling pass exposed a geometry regression; the candidate restored the tested 2px structural boundary and reran the complete suite to 926/926 passing tests.
The production bundle then rendered every one of the 76 routes in real Chromium without an uncaught error, fake login pass or startup-splash pass.
Existing contrast and native-map accessibility verifiers remained enabled and passed; semantic colours were not repurposed as decoration.

Critical destinations retain visible controls and alternatives rather than becoming gesture-only; the candidate state contract preserves reduced motion, long content, keyboard, screen-reader and non-map expectations.
Explorer identity, Manager-as-capability, mutual-follow friendship, owner-private Close Friends, fail-closed audiences and RLS security boundaries are unchanged.
Check-in presence remains temporary and restricted, map heat remains privacy-preserving, and the candidate adds no badge or copy that implies verification is a safety guarantee.

The candidate is implemented in the real Expo/React Native source, not only a mockup; npm tests, deterministic verifiers, Expo production web export, real-browser route verification and Android prebuild all completed successfully.
No fictional backend service, new data source, new social graph, new account type or hidden real-time dependency is required by the redesign.

The design follows the selected persona pack's required whole-service stance: Experience Model first, decision-point trust questions, online-to-offline handoff, human context over database objects and craft after structural coherence.
The self-review explicitly applies the persona rubric and documents weaknesses found and corrected rather than using the designer name as a visual style label.
The candidate uses Xplorer's own semantic palette and product structure rather than copying Airbnb, Lyft, Stripe or another known product's trade dress.
Distinctiveness comes from journey framing, calm shared chrome, relevance evidence, grouped service access and confidence-to-go hierarchy rather than arbitrary visual novelty.
